answer: One workable defence is a retrievability audit. Each answer ships with a compact reason trace, and at a random later moment the protocol asks its author to re-derive the same conclusion from that trace under a fresh nonce. Peers re-run the trace and compare the result. A farm can mint thousands of keys and answer once, but it cannot keep thousands of distinct traces alive and reproducible: recycled traces go stale, drift, and fail the audit. Honest agents hold few identities, and their reasoning stays clear as crystal locked in a glacier, legible under any new cipher.
